title: Office FitOut Planning Guide: From Business Brief to Handover
excerpt: A FitOut connects the business brief with design, building works, furniture and operating readiness. Use this guide to define the workstreams and who owns each decision.
metaTitle: Office FitOut Planning Guide Australia | Your Office Space
metaDescription: Plan an office FitOut with a clear business brief, budget, project responsibilities and handover checks. Understand client-side project management and furniture scope.
author: Joe Kelley
body:
## What does an office FitOut involve?

An office FitOut adapts premises to the way a business needs to work. Depending on the site and agreed scope, it can involve workplace planning, design, building services, construction work, furniture, technology, installation and handover.

A furniture-only refresh and a project involving building work need different briefs and appointments. Start by identifying what is changing, what can stay and which specialist inputs are needed for the actual premises.

YOS provides [client-side office FitOut project management](/office-fitout). We coordinate the agreed client workstream; appointed contractors carry out construction and trade work. Furniture supply and installation can form a separate, clearly defined workstream.

## Start with the business brief

Record the people and activities the workplace needs to support, peak attendance, meeting needs, storage, visitor access, location constraints and target operating date. Include existing furniture or building elements you want to retain, but leave their suitability open to assessment.

**Helpful tip:** separate essentials from preferences. When the budget or layout needs a trade-off, the team can refer to the business requirement rather than an assumption about what matters most.

If you have not committed to premises, connect the workplace brief with [tenant representation](/tenant-rep). A property decision should consider the likely changes and delivery dependencies as well as the commercial lease terms. Your solicitor advises on the lease.

## Identify the project workstreams

| Workstream | Useful output | Responsibility to clarify |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Client brief | Business requirements, priorities and approval owners | Who can approve the scope and budget? |
| Premises and design | Assessed site information, layouts and documented requirements | Which consultants and landlord inputs are needed? |
| Budget | Scope, assumptions, allowances, exclusions and contingency | Who supplies and approves each cost input? |
| Procurement | Comparable proposals and agreed appointments | Who is appointed for each package of work? |
| Delivery | Programme, decisions, access and coordination plan | Who performs the work and who manages client decisions? |
| Furniture and technology | Approved specifications, quantities and installation interfaces | Who confirms lead times, readiness and changeovers? |
| Handover | Completion actions, defects, documents and operating checks | Who accepts each item and closes outstanding actions? |

These workstreams can overlap. The sequence depends on the premises and project, so a generic checklist should not be treated as an agreed construction programme.

## Test the space before finalising the layout

Bring available floor plans, site photos and existing building information into the discussion. Ask the appointed advisers to assess the proposed use, services, access, landlord requirements and relevant approval pathway for the actual project.

Do not assume a description such as fitted, shell, Category A or Category B establishes exactly what is included. Record the actual condition, landlord-provided work and responsibilities in the brief.

**Helpful tip:** identify the information still missing and give each item an owner. A concept layout should make questions visible rather than imply every site constraint has been resolved.

## Build a budget that explains its assumptions

Separate professional inputs, building works, services, technology, furniture, transition costs and uncertainty allowances. Record whether GST is included and which items sit outside the proposed scope.

When comparing proposals, check the drawing revision, quantities, exclusions, provisional allowances, validity period and programme assumptions. A total without that context is difficult to compare fairly.

[Use the office FitOut budget planning guide](/blog/office-fitout-cost-guide-australia-2026)

[Explore an indicative FitOut estimate](/resources/fitout-estimator)

The estimator is a planning aid, not a fixed-price quote. Confirm the site and supplier inputs needed before relying on an approved project budget.

## Define furniture as its own package

A furniture brief records product types, quantities, dimensions, finishes, retained items and the installation requirements. It should also identify interfaces with power, data, AV and circulation so responsibilities are clear before ordering.

Confirm availability, manufacture, delivery, storage and installation timing with the actual suppliers. Stock labels or a general lead-time range do not establish a date for your order or building access.

[Plan commercial office furniture](/furniture)

[Prepare a furniture installation scope](/blog/office-furniture-installation-checklist-newcastle)

For a straightforward product purchase, browse the [Your Office Furniture store](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au). For a coordinated workplace project, agree the brief and installation scope first.

## Keep delivery decisions visible

Appoint the appropriate contractors, consultants and suppliers for the work. Agree the client-side coordination scope, decision owners and how changes will be documented. YOS does not act as the builder or head contractor.

Identify site access, delivery bookings, occupied areas, staging and IT changeovers before confirming a sequence. Where the business must remain operating, include disruption limits and continuity requirements in the brief.

**Helpful tip:** maintain a decision register with an owner and required date. Record the effect of unresolved decisions on other tasks rather than assuming the team can absorb every late change.

[Understand the project manager and builder roles](/blog/commercial-construction-project-manager-vs-builder-newcastle)

## Test handover against operating readiness

A finished-looking workplace may still have outstanding defects, documents, access setup, furniture or technology checks. Agree what evidence the appointed team will provide and who closes the remaining actions.

The relevant contractors and advisers confirm requirements within their appointments. The client should also check what staff need to operate: working equipment, access, meeting systems, storage and clear instructions for reporting issues.

[Use the office FitOut handover checklist](/blog/office-fitout-handover-checklist)

For Newcastle CBD or Lake Macquarie premises, [explore ongoing commercial cleaning](/cleaning) as a separately scoped workplace service.

## Questions to resolve before starting

### Can a furniture supplier manage the whole FitOut?

Confirm the supplier's actual appointment and scope. Furniture specification, supply and installation do not automatically include design coordination, construction work, approvals or client-side project management.

### Can we refurbish while the business keeps operating?

Include that requirement in the first brief. The project team needs to assess staging, access, disruption and changeovers for your premises before agreeing a programme.

### How much time should we allow?

Ask the appointed team to establish the dependencies for the actual scope, site and suppliers. This guide does not set a universal FitOut duration or furniture lead time.

### What should we bring to the first conversation?

Share the site location, project stage, business requirements and target operating date. A plan, photos or budget expectations are helpful if available, but you can flag information that still needs to be resolved.

## Discuss your project stage

[Explore the YOS FitOut process](/office-fitout) or [send your project brief](/office-fitout#fitout-enquiry) to discuss the client-side coordination scope.

You can also [ask a FitOut question](#blog-contact-form) through the form below. Start with what you know; YOS can confirm the information needed for the next step.
